lessons.title: A speed, not a frame count
body: Adding the same amount every frame makes an animation faster on screens with higher refresh rates. Multiplying by elapsed seconds gives a rate such as radians per second.

The workspace caps delta after long interruptions to avoid sudden simulation jumps. Change the speed below. The motion should remain recognizable when the preview is resized or when the display refresh rate changes.
lessons.task: Set angularSpeed to 1.2 radians per second.
lessons.hint: Keep the multiplication by delta inside onFrame.

quiz.question: For two radians per second, add…
quiz.explanation: A rate multiplied by time gives the amount of change.

lessons.title: A gentle floating motion
body: Math.sin returns a smooth repeating value between -1 and 1. Multiplying by an amplitude sets the travel distance on either side of the center.

The time multiplier controls angular frequency. At elapsed * 2, a full cycle takes π seconds because sine repeats every 2π radians. Using elapsed time sets the position directly, preventing accumulated drift.
lessons.hint: The sphere will move between Y = -0.75 and Y = 0.75.

lessons.title: Draw a circle with time
body: Sine and cosine are offset by a quarter turn. Use cosine for X and sine for Z to place an object on a horizontal circle.

Multiplying both coordinates by the same radius preserves a circular orbit. Different multipliers produce an ellipse. The parent group approach from earlier is another way to create an orbit; these coordinates make the mathematics explicit.
lessons.hint: Change the radius variable. Both sine and cosine use it.

quiz.question: Equal sine and cosine amplitudes create…
quiz.explanation: The paired coordinates lie on a circle because sin²(t) + cos²(t) = 1.

lessons.title: Make a movement feel natural
body: Linear interpolation moves at a constant rate. An easing function remaps progress to change that rate while keeping the same endpoints.

Smoothstep uses t²(3−2t) for t between 0 and 1. It starts slowly, accelerates through the middle, and slows near the end. This loop moves back and forth; enable easing and watch how it approaches each marker.
lessons.hint: The smoothstep formula is already written. Enable its branch.

quiz.question: Easing changes…
options: The mapping from time to progress
quiz.explanation: Easing shapes the speed profile of a transition.

lessons.title: Turn smoothly in 3D
body: Euler angles are convenient, but interpolating three separate angles can create awkward rotations. Quaternions represent orientation in a form well suited to interpolation and composition.

slerpQuaternions interpolates between two orientations along a spherical path. Build a target orientation from a normalized axis and an angle, then smoothly approach it. You rarely need to manipulate the four quaternion components directly.
lessons.hint: The target is a half turn around the normalized (1, 1, 0) axis.

quiz.question: What is slerp useful for?
quiz.explanation: Spherical interpolation is useful for interpolating rotations.
